avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates platelet aggregation effects and may increase thrombotic risk when combined with oprelvekin's platelet-stimulating activity
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; discontinue ginkgo biloba at least 2 weeks before oprelvekin therapy

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic supplements (concentrated)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: High-dose garlic may enhance antiplatelet effects leading to unpredictable hemostasis when combined with oprelvekin-induced platelet proliferation
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid therapeutic garlic supplements; culinary garlic is acceptable

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin E (>400 IU daily)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet effects that could theoretically interact with oprelvekin's thrombotic potential
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for unusual bleeding or clotting; maintain standard supplementation levels

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (fish oil)
caution_supplements.mechanism: High-dose fish oil may have mild anticoagulant properties; clinical significance unclear with oprelvekin
caution_supplements.action: Monitor hemostasis; standard supplementation is likely safe

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Oprelvekin can cause fluid retention and hypertension; excessive sodium may exacerbate these effects
caution_foods.action: Encourage moderate sodium intake and monitor blood pressure regularly

monitoring_notes: Oprelvekin undergoes minimal hepatic metabolism and has no significant CYP450 interactions, reducing traditional drug-supplement interactions. Monitor for signs of thrombosis, fluid retention, and hypertension, which are the primary concerns when combining with supplements affecting platelet function or fluid balance.
